title: Establish retry contract and idempotency guardrails for SDKs and services
creator: Anjali Rao
description: Goal: Define a single, implementable retry/timeout/backoff contract and idempotency/hedging guardrails that both Redwood services and official SDKs (JS, Python, Go) will adopt. This is to reduce cross-service SLO flakiness during multi-region failover and load-shedding events, enable safe hedged requests where appropriate, and standardize circuit-breaker signals so platform automation and customers have predictable behavior.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Documented retry contract published in Confluence + link in SDK READMEs. 2) SDKs implement the new default retry/backoff/timeouts with configurable overrides. 3) Service-side libraries accept `Idempotency-Key` and deduplicate by default for mutating endpoints when supplied. 4) Hedging only enabled by SDK when endpoint advertises idempotency support or for non-mutating reads; integration tests to prove no double-side effects. 5) Circuit-breaker and load-shed signals standardized via headers/metrics (see spec below) and visible in Console dashboards. 6) Canary rollout across 10% -> 50% -> 100% with canary+rollback runbook complete.
spec_summary: Client-side defaults: exponential backoff with full jitter, base=100ms, max_interval=5s, max_retries=3 for idempotent requests; for non-idempotent requests default max_retries=0 unless `Idempotency-Key` provided. Timeouts: interactive=1s, standard=5s, long=30s. Hedging: allow 1 additional hedged request after hedging_delay=75ms only for endpoints marked as hedgable or when client provides an idempotency key. Server-side behavior: respect `Idempotency-Key` header, return 409 on duplicate conflict only when necessary, include `X-Redwood-Request-Id` and `X-Redwood-Idempotency-Status` headers. Load-shedding: respond 429 or 503 with `Retry-After` and `X-Redwood-Load-Shed:true`. Circuit-breaker: `X-Redwood-Circuit-Open:true` when the breaker is tripped. Metrics: `service.{svc}.retry_{outcome}`, `service.{svc}.circuit_open_count`, `service.{svc}.hedge_attempts`, `service.{svc}.idempotency_conflicts`.
migration_plan: Phase 1 (Docs + Spec): publish contract and SDK PR templates (this ticket). Phase 2 (SDK): implement defaults behind runtime-configurable flags; release minor SDK versions with opt-in. Phase 3 (Services): library support for idempotency header + dedupe storage; accept both old and new header formats for 90 days. Phase 4 (Canary): enable in runtime for 10% of traffic for 2 days, collect metrics/dashboards; expand to 50% if no regression; full rollout after 1 week stable. Phase 5 (Cleanup): deprecate legacy behavior and remove backwards compatibility after 3 months. Rollback plan: flip SDK flag and service feature flag; console alerts and paging on SLO regression.
implementation_notes: Adopt full jitter per AWS Exponential Backoff recommendations to avoid thundering herd.
Clients MUST never retry on 4xx (except 429) unless explicitly configured.
Hedging only for endpoints that are idempotent or where server will dedupe based on a request token.
Services should annotate OpenAPI specs with `x-redwood-hedge: true` and `x-redwood-idempotent: true` to allow SDK automation.
Circuit-breaker state exposed in response headers and metrics to help Console auto-annotate incident timelines.
Add unit + integration tests that simulate multi-region failover (delays + 500s) to validate no double-posts under hedging + idempotency.
Create a compatibility shim in the Node/Python SDKs to gracefully accept legacy retry settings.
Instrumentation: correlate client-side retry attempts with server-side dedupe outcomes using `X-Redwood-Request-Id`.
Performance: ensure retry/backoff defaults keep p50 latency within SLO for interactive routes under normal load.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Hedged requests could cause double side-effects if servers don't dedupe. Mitigation: default hedging OFF unless idempotency token present; require service opt-in via OpenAPI annotation.

Risk: Too-aggressive retry policies increase costs and overload backend. Mitigation: conservative defaults (max_retries=3 idempotent), full jitter, circuit-breaker thresholds and load-shed signals to short-circuit retries.
Risk: Backwards compatibility with older SDKs and services. Mitigation: accept legacy headers, introduce runtime feature flagging, and provide migration docs + compatibility shim in SDKs.
Risk: Monitoring blindspots during rollout. Mitigation: create dedicated dashboards and SLO alerts before canary rollout; require green on synthetic test suite.

2026-02-24 Priya Desai (Security): Approved storing ephemeral dedupe tokens for up to 24 hours; recommended encryption at rest and KMS usage for dedupe keys. Added security checklist to `implementation_notes`.
2026-02-28 Evan Kim (SDK lead): Implemented Node SDK compatibility shim in feature branch. Initial tests pass against mock server but failing one integration test for hedging ordering; investigating.

2026-03-02 Marcus Li: Ran synthetic multi-region failover test against staging; observed reduced SLO violations for interactive routes but a spike in cost for heavy hedging - adjusted hedging_delay upward and lowered default hedging to disabled.
2026-03-04 Platform: Infra needs ETS export for `service.*.hedge_attempts` metric before canary. Blocker created: ENG-8450. We've added ENG-8450 to dependencies.
